node_definition.done_when: Read section 8 of a-page-load-reads-each-file-once first. First reproduce the defect at your base. A test copies the reckon package into a temporary directory, starts a server from that copy, and edits the copy on disk so that a lazily imported name appears which the in-memory module lacks. It then requests a route that triggers the lazy import, and at your base the response is a 500 carrying an ImportError. The test never edits a file in the repository. After the change, a running server either reloads onto one consistent revision when its code changes, or refuses that request with a named, visible stale-code error whose status and body name stale-code and both code fingerprints, rather than a mid-request ImportError. Reuse the code stamp the watch producer already computes for its own reload (grep reckon/ for code_stamp) rather than a second fingerprint. tests/test_server_serves_one_code_version.py carries the case, which fails at your base. Existing tests reaching reckon/serve.py keep passing; grep tests/ for serve and the server's handler entry points to build the gate. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/a-page-load-reads-each-file-once/server-serves-one-code-version.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line as revision= followed by the full sha, and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
